title: Pinned integral open coefficient and operation presentation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], completed coefficient rings $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_{n+1})_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and ringed sequence sites with their actual quotient transitions [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Define the open object to be $j$ in $X_{proet}$ and the slice-site functor to send an object over $j$ to the corresponding object over $U$.
A coefficient presentation consists of finite coefficient maps from the restriction to this slice to the continuous pushforward from $U$, taking every constant section to the same constant section; a completed coefficient map commuting with every quotient projection; equivalences of integral module categories and of finite module categories whose forward functors are the concrete continuous pushforwards with those coefficient maps; and a whole-system equivalence whose forward functor is the continuous sequence-site pushforward, whose coefficient map has exactly the specified finite components. An operation presentation adds additivity for all three kinds of equivalence, the concrete localized open-system extension, and evaluation comparison isomorphisms which act as the identity on underlying sections. No existence is asserted.
For such a presentation $o$, define ordinary extension as its integral equivalence followed by the section-normalized localized extension [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and ordinary restriction as localized restriction followed by the inverse equivalence. Their adjunction is the composite of the equivalence adjunction and the actual localized extension/restriction adjunction. Define $j_!$ and $j^*$ on derived categories by applying these exact functors termwise and localizing [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]; the derived open adjunction is that localization, retaining the ordinary unit and counit.
